attachment.snippet:
1	// A member's own task declarations state their scheduling in the current vocabulary
2	// (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §5, #1725). Two rewrites over every
3	// `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/tasks/<name>/task.json`: the retired `frequency`
4	// field folded into `preconditions` — `due:<cadence>` first in the list, a `none`
5	// beside it dropped, and `manual` (no schedule) folded into no list at all — and
6	// then the `trigger` its conditions already implied, stated outright. Both as
7	// anchored text, so the file's own layout survives.
8	//
9	// THE WRITE IS THE ENGINE'S. `updateTaskSchedulingFields: true` names the registry's
10	// named codemod (engine/migrations/registry.mjs, `applyTaskSchedulingFields`), which
11	// runs the same rewrite the CLI does. A record cannot carry it: which files hold
12	// which field is the member's own disk.
13	//
14	// GATED ON THE MOUNT, BY CONTENT. Rewriting is only safe once the member's vendored
15	// `claudinite-tasks` reads the cadence term — the door in its task-contract turns
16	// `frequency` into that term, and its calendar spells the term; an older mount
17	// would validate `due:daily` as an unknown condition and skip the task. The two
18	// lanes deliver on their own cadences, so `appliesTo` probes the mounted calendar
19	// for the spelling rather than trusting the stamp; an unreadable mount reads as
20	// "not capable" and the record stays inert. The canon runs the same probe against
21	// its own tree (two-root form).
22	//
23	// IDEMPOTENT by construction: a task.json with no `frequency` line and a stated
24	// `trigger` is nothing to rewrite. No apply stage: the rewrite is text, and a
25	// session has nothing to add.
26	const CALENDAR = 'packs/claudinite-tasks/calendar.mjs';
27	const mountReadsCadence = async (read) => {
28	  const text = (await read(`.claudinite/shared/${CALENDAR}`)) ?? (await read(CALENDAR));
29	  return Boolean(text) && text.includes('cadenceTermFor');
30	};
31	
32	export default {
33	  id: 'task-cadence-terms',
34	  landed: '2026-09-05',
35	  // The version is cut on main after the merge (#1726), so a record cannot name it
36	  // exactly: this is the next number the bump cuts for the pack at 60906.4 — above
37	  // every member's installed version, so the gap holds the record, and never above
38	  // the number cut, so a converged member does not re-apply it.
39	  version: '60906.5',
40	  summary: 'a member\'s local-pack task.json declarations fold the retired `frequency` field into `preconditions` as the cadence term it meant, and state the `trigger` their conditions implied (#1725)',
41	
42	  appliesTo: mountReadsCadence,
43	  updateTaskSchedulingFields: true,
44	
45	  // The telemetry hook cannot list directories, and what this record retires — a
46	  // `frequency` line, and an unstated `trigger`, under the member's local packs — is
47	  // only visible by listing. The fleet-visible signal is the `legacy-task-fields`
48	  // advisory on each; the doors' removal is gated on that advisory's convergence
49	  // window (#1732 for the field, #1789 for the derivation).
50	  legacyPresent: async () => false,
51	};

input.command:
git add -A engine/ engine-tests/ packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/ && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
The nightly update states a member's trigger as well as folding its frequency

A member's own task declarations are its author's, so the field they must now
carry has to arrive by the same route the cadence term does. The record's rewrite
becomes two anchored-text patches over one file: the retired `frequency` folded
into `preconditions`, and then the `trigger` those conditions already implied.

The patch goes BEFORE an anchor key, never after one, because the last key of an
object carries no comma — `preconditions` where the file has it, `expected_outcome`
otherwise, since the contract requires that one. A one-line object keeps its own
separator.

The probe now reads both the mounted calendar and the mounted schema: an older
calendar validates `due:daily` as an unknown condition, and an older schema is
`additionalProperties: false`, so a trigger written into it is an illegal key in
the author's editor. Either half alone leaves the record inert.

Refs #1725

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Vx66tEVdGCKBRryHprSRLv
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short

the stub — `packs/claudinite-tasks/hash-minute.mjs`, a pure function of the repo full name that
  bootstrap stamps in and baselining re-derives), a `concurrency` group, a
  `workflow_dispatch` trigger (whose one `wake` input is how a task is forced,
  here or from another repo), and a call into the vendored scheduler run — no logic of its own
  (schema and behaviour changes ride the vendor refresh, not workflow edits). It
  is the repo's **only** cron; the executor's workflow beside it carries none. Work
  that had its own cron'd workflow becomes a **task**, and that workflow is deleted
  — its steps move into the task's worker. So does work with no cron at all: an
  event-driven or condition-gated job becomes a task with no `preconditions` (a
  declaration with none is not on the schedule), woken by whatever knows the
  event happened.
  Don't keep either as a dispatch-only workflow for the task to fire: that is two files and two edit sites for one job, and a
  workflow whose only caller is the thing that replaced it. (The exception is narrow,
  and it is **not** about privilege. An Actions-only secret is reachable from
  code-work, which runs Action-side — `code_work_required_secrets`, below. A deploy target's
  OIDC identity is one `permissions:` line in the executor's own workflow, not a wall.
  A one-shot external effect is handled by `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'`, not by
  escaping to a workflow. What genuinely does not fit is the Actions **composition
```json
"preconditions": ["due:weekly", "substantive-change", "commits-outside:.claudinite/"]
```

**The first condition says when.** Every scheduler tick asks every task that has
an expression, so the expression is the whole of a task's schedule — and a task
with no `preconditions` has no schedule: the scheduler never asks it, and it runs
only from a hand-created item, a mark, a `--wake` or a chain link, where the empty
expression holds at pick (what the retired `frequency: manual` meant). Write no
term for "somebody created my item": that is true of every run, so it states
nothing; and `none` is retired, an explicit empty marker being a second spelling
of absence. Three built-ins read the task's own run history (its
unqualified `[claudinite-work]` items over the last 40 days), and they are judged
before anything else is collected, so a task whose cadence declines costs no read:

- `due:<daily|weekly|monthly>` — no run since that cadence's most recent anchor on
  the repo's `taskScheduler` schedule; fixed hours, so the hour never drifts.
- `last-run-over:<12h|1d|7d>` — the newest run started more than that long ago;
  the hour drifts by up to a tick's gap each period.
- `last-run-not-failed` — the newest run does not stand at a failure park.
  Declare it where a run past the task's own failure would repeat the fault;
  absent it, the next occurrence is filed beside the park.

A `due:` or `last-run-over:` term holds on a woken item — the wake stands in for
the cadence — while every other condition still applies. A task with a movement
condition and no cadence term is legal and runs whenever the movement is there, at
most once per tick. One more shape has no schedule, structurally: a term that reads
the item itself (`needsItem`, which only the built-in request implementer's
`request-eligible` declares) has nothing to be judged against at a tick, so
`isScheduledTask` leaves that task to its items too. A declaration still carrying
`frequency` is rewritten into its cadence term at the door (`manual` drops to no
expression) and reported by `legacy-task-fields`: write the term.

**`preconditions` is the only gate there is.** The `precondition` function and its
`precondition_signals` companion are retired: both are rejected by name, and the
signal union is derived from the conditions — each names what it reads, so the
collector can never disagree with the gate. A gate the built-ins cannot express is
a **task-local term** in a `preconditions.mjs` beside the declaration, which is
handed `{ arg, config, item, windowDays, now, schedule }` and stays pure over them.

**Three things are NOT preconditions**, and putting them there is the common

    alternatives, and why each lost:

      the scheduler wrote, and everything it prevented — re-asking a declined
      occurrence — the history terms prevent for free by reading the queue the
      run already holds: a `due:` task that ran declines on its history at no
      read, and one that declined is simply asked again, which costs nothing
      where the cadence decides. What the board added was a second authority
      over "did this period happen", a parse/serialize module, a write per
      changed row, a closed-issue lookup path, and a class of degradations
      (absent row, mangled body, reopened board) to reason about.

      task's lane" was one rule the engine applied to every task; it was right
      for a task that breaks the same way each period and wrong for one whose

The corpus states the trigger where it stated the shape of an expression

Eighteen places said a task is off the schedule when it states no condition, or
one that reads the item. That was true for a window and is not the rule any more,
so each says what it now is: `trigger` decides who asks, `preconditions` decides
what must hold, and the conditions are judged the same way whether the scheduler
or a person produced the occurrence.

the `woken` term, and — new — the shape of `preconditions` as the signal, with
the ground it lost on and the structural classifier weighed against it.

Refs #1725

The simulator models the trigger, and finds a cadence on a request task is inert

The sim carried its own copy of the structural rule, so it now carries its own
copy of the trigger door — deliberately, since what it models is what the engine
WRITES. Neutering that door turns 59 of its scenarios red, so it is modelling the
field rather than agreeing with it by construction.

Writing S79 for the shapes the old rule could not state turned one of them up as
a defect. A cadence term on a `request` task cannot hold anything back: nothing
asks such a task, so every occurrence of it is an item somebody created, every
such item carries `Woken:`, and a wake stands in for the cadence. The term
declines no run and reads as though it limits the lever, so
`task-declaration-shape` rejects the pairing outright — my first draft of the
scenario asserted the opposite and the sim disagreed.

Refs #1725

content.text:
{"number":1733,"title":"Scheduling is the task's own precondition; the scheduler keeps no state","body":"Phase 1 of #1725: every scheduler tick asks every task that states a condition, and the task's own `preconditions` carry the whole answer. The engine keeps no scheduling state and no calendar of its own.

## The vocabulary

| term | holds when |
|---|---|
| `due:<daily\|weekly\|monthly>` | no run of the task started or ended since that cadence's most recent anchor on the repo's schedule |
| `last-run-over:<12h\|1d\|7d>` | the task's newest run started more than that long ago, or none in the 40-day horizon |
| `last-run-not-failed` | the task's newest run is not at a failure park — the opt-in that stops a task past its own failure |

`preconditions` is optional. **Absent or empty means the task is not on the schedule**: the scheduler never asks it, and it runs only from an item somebody creates (a mark, a hand-created item, a `--wake`, a chain link, a fan-out target), at whose pick the empty expression holds. A term that reads the item itself (`request-eligible`, `needsItem: true`) keeps its task off the schedule the same way — nothing to judge at a tick. `isScheduledTask(decl, terms)` decides both. The `woken` term the first commit introduced was retired on review: "somebody created my item" is true of every run, so as a precondition it said nothing.

`frequency` and `none` are retired. The contract's door reads a legacy `frequency` as the cadence term it meant (first in `preconditions`, a `none` beside it dropped, the field deleted; `manual` adds no term); `legacy-task-fields` advises the field and `task-declaration-shape` names the edit. The `task-cadence-terms` migration record folds the field into members' own local `task.json` files as anchored text on their nightly update; #1732 retires the door after the window. (#1783 records that a record can no longer name the version the bump cuts on `main`; this record names the next number for the pack as it stands.)

## The mechanism

- A new `runs` signal — the task's own unqualified work items an executor picked, newest first, the item under evaluation excluded — is what the three terms read, and it sets every other signal's window to "since this task's newest run that actually ran" (a rejected item does not move it), falling back to the cadence's period plus an hour with no run in the horizon. **A run begins at the pick**: an item still wearing `blocked` or `waiting-for-executor`, open or closed, is not a run (the simulator found F32: a deduped twin, or a still-waiting sibling, read as this period's run and the survivor declined at its pick).
- The scheduler run asks every scheduled task at every tick. The run-history terms are judged first, over the queue the run already fetched, so a task whose cadence declines collects nothing else; only an undecided ask collects the task's other signals. A yes files a ready planned item, a no is one log line (`asked <task>: no — <reason>`), an ask the scheduler cannot decide fails open. At a pick the executor reads the history only where a term or a windowed collector reads it.
- One live item per task is the engine's only invariant. A parked item (any kind, failure included) is not live: the next occurrence is filed beside it unless the task declares `last-run-not-failed`. The schedule board, the first-window booking, the sleeping-item migration and the engine-owned lane hold are deleted.
- Hand-created items, forced mints and `--wake` stamp `Woken:`; the cadence terms hold on a woken item (the wake stands in for the cadence) while every other condition still applies. `itemFacts` treats any item that is not the scheduler's own unqualified planned item as woken.
- The executor re-evaluates at pick as before, over the item's facts and the repo schedule; a decline still closes the item `rejected`.

Every canon declaration is converted (`daily` → `due:daily`, `weekly` → `due:weekly`, `monthly` → `due:monthly`; the four `manual` tasks carry no `preconditions`; the request implementer carries `["request-eligible"]`). Pack versions are not bumped here — `pack-version-bump` cuts them on `main`.

## What changed where

input.body:
Phase 1 of #1725: every scheduler tick asks every scheduled task, and the task's own declaration carries the whole answer. The engine keeps no scheduling state and no calendar of its own.

## Two fields, one sentence

`trigger` says **who mints an occurrence**; `preconditions` says **what must then hold**.

- `trigger: "schedule"` — asked by the scheduler at every tick.
- `trigger: "request"` — asked by nobody. It runs only from an item somebody creates (a mark, a hand-created item, a `--wake`, a chain link, a fan-out target), at whose pick its conditions are judged *exactly* as a scheduled task's are.

`isScheduledTask(decl)` is now a field read — no terms to load, no shape to interpret. `preconditions` stays optional and means only "requires nothing".

| term | holds when |
|---|---|
| `due:<daily\|weekly\|monthly>` | no run of the task started or ended since that cadence's most recent anchor on the repo's schedule |
| `last-run-over:<12h\|1d\|7d>` | the task's newest run started more than that long ago, or none in the 40-day horizon |
| `last-run-not-failed` | the task's newest run is not at a failure park — the opt-in that stops a task past its own failure |

Two earlier spellings of this were tried and are recorded in DESIGN §15.33 with the ground each lost on: a `woken` term (retired on review — "somebody created my item" is true of every run), and then the **shape** of `preconditions` (retired on review as cryptic: `["none"]` and no key at all were a keystroke apart and meant opposite things, and it made a scheduling question need the task's own terms loaded to answer, which is how one call site came to answer it wrong).

Two pairings the shape could not have caught, both now rejected by `task-declaration-shape`:

- A `schedule` task whose condition reads the item itself — the tick carries no item, so the term errors every hour instead of declining.
- A `request` task carrying a cadence term. **Writing S79 turned this up as a defect:** every occurrence of a request task is one somebody created, every such item carries `Woken:`, and a wake stands in for the cadence — so the term declines no run and only reads as though it limits the lever. My first draft of the scenario asserted the opposite and the simulator disagreed.

## An origin of its own

`task:origin:ad-hoc` carried two unlike things. `task:origin:manual` is now the second: an occurrence of a **declared task** somebody pulled the lever on, as against somebody's own issue adopted as the work item itself. Both stay exempt from the janitor's supersede rule, for reasons the comment now gives separately — an ad-hoc park because every ad-hoc item runs the same task over a different subject (#1498), a manual park because a pulled run is usually scoped by a qualifier the task's next clean occurrence did not cover. The dashboard's flows lane, which exists to show what people asked for, shows both.

## Retired, and how members converge

`frequency` and `none` are retired. The contract's door reads a legacy `frequency` as the cadence term plus the trigger it always meant (`manual` → `trigger: "request"` and no term), and derives `trigger` for a declaration stating none from exactly what the predicate read before — verified against all 28 canon declarations before they were given the field, so nothing changed behaviour. `legacy-task-fields` reports both; the `task-cadence-terms` record writes both into members' own local `task.json` files as anchored text on their nightly update, gated on the member's mount reading *both* (an older calendar rejects `due:daily`; an older schema is `additionalProperties: false` and would call a stated trigger an illegal key). #1732 retires the field door, #1789 the trigger derivation.

## The mechanism

- A `runs` signal — the task's own unqualified work items an executor picked, newest first, the item under evaluation excluded — is what the three terms read, and it sets every other signal's window. **A run begins at the pick**: an item still wearing `blocked` or `waiting-for-executor`, open or closed, is not a run (the simulator found F32).
- The run-history terms are judged first, over the queue the run already fetched, so a task whose cadence declines collects nothing else. A yes files a ready planned item, a no is one log line, an ask the scheduler cannot decide fails open.
- One live item per task is the engine's only invariant. A parked item is not live: the next occurrence is filed beside it unless the task declares `last-run-not-failed`. The schedule board, the first-window booking and the engine-owned lane hold are deleted.
- Rebasing brought in rule I (#1785), whose standing test was passing a frequency string into a predicate that now takes a boolean — so it silently stopped firing. Re-typed, and its posted comment no longer promises to release a lane that a park no longer holds.

## What changed where

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — `task-contract.mjs` (the two doors, `TRIGGERS`, `isScheduledTask`), `task.schema.json`, `calendar.mjs`, `precondition-policy.mjs`, `discover.mjs` (terms loaded before the door, so it can see them), the two checks, `signals/`, `queue/` (stateless run, `Woken:`, `itemFacts`, `ORIGIN_MANUAL`, janitor), the migration record; tests for all of it.
- `engine/migrations/` — the anchored-text rewrite, now both fields, and its registry op.
- Every pack's `tasks/*/task.json`, and the per-pack tests and READMEs.
- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/` — the roster reads the trigger, with the page's own copy of the door pinned to the contract's over one vector set.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md` — the simulator models the field as the engine writes it (neutering its door turns 59 scenarios red); S74–S79.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §5 and §15.33, `docs/task-preconditions/DESIGN.md`, the `writing-tasks` skill.

Closes #1731

Two more phase-1 divergences from the plan, on the owner's review of [#1733](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1733).

**The shape of `preconditions` is no longer the scheduling signal.** Retiring `woken` left absence carrying the meaning, and the owner ruled that cryptic: `["none"]` and no key at all were a keystroke apart and meant opposite things, and it made "is this task scheduled?" need the task's own terms loaded to answer — which is how one call site came to answer it wrong. A declaration now states `trigger: schedule | request`, and `preconditions` says only what must hold, judged identically whichever produced the occurrence. Both rejected alternatives (the `woken` term, and the shape) are recorded in DESIGN §15.33 with the ground each lost on, including the structural classifier weighed against the field.

The door derives `trigger` for a declaration stating none, from exactly what the predicate read before — verified against all 28 canon declarations before they were given the field. [#1789](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1789) retires that derivation, on the same convergence window [#1732](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1732) waits on.

**`task:origin:manual`.** `ad-hoc` carried both somebody's own issue adopted as the work item and a pulled run of a declared task; the second is now its own origin. Both stay exempt from the janitor's supersede rule, for reasons that are now stated separately.

**One defect found while writing the scenario for it.** A cadence term on a `request` task is inert, not a rate limit: every occurrence of such a task is one somebody created, every such item carries `Woken:`, and a wake stands in for the cadence. It declines no run and reads as though it limits the lever, so `task-declaration-shape` rejects the pairing. My first draft of S79 asserted the opposite and the simulator disagreed.

Comment class: correction, feature — the implicit signal was the correction, the explicit field and the origin label the feature. Both landed on [PR #1733](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1733).

You were right that absence was doing load-bearing work, and it was worse than the one case you named: there were *two* implicit routes off the schedule — no `preconditions`, and a term that reads the item — and answering "is this scheduled?" needed the task's own `preconditions.mjs` loaded, which is how one call site came to answer it wrong earlier in this branch. `isScheduledTask(decl)` is now a field read.

I went with `trigger: schedule | request` over your `cadence: scheduled | manual`, per the popup: the rate lives in `due:weekly` next door, and `manual` would revive the value we just retired from `frequency`. The door derives it for a legacy declaration from exactly what the predicate read before — I checked all 28 canon declarations against the derivation before giving them the field, so nothing changed behaviour.

Two things I got wrong along the way, both caught by writing the proof rather than by review:

- I told you in the popup that `origin:manual` would fix the janitor. Reading `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS` and #1498, that would have **reintroduced** the bug — a pulled run is usually scoped by a qualifier the next clean occurrence didn't cover. Both origins stay exempt; the label's value is that the two now state their different reasons.
- Writing scenario S79, I asserted that a cadence on a `request` task rate-limits the lever. The simulator disagreed: every occurrence of a request task is `Woken`-stamped, and a wake stands in for the cadence, so the term declines *nothing* and only reads as though it limits something. That's a blocking check now.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/          trigger vocabulary, the two doors, isScheduledTask as a field
                                 read; schema; ORIGIN_MANUAL; discover loads terms before the
                                 door so it can see them; both checks gain a trigger half
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/    createWorkItem stamps manual; janitor exempts both asked-for
                                 origins; rule I re-typed after the rebase
engine/migrations/               the nightly rewrite states the trigger as well as folding the
                                 frequency; probe now needs the mount to read both
packs/claudinite-dashboard/      roster reads the trigger; the page's copy of the door pinned
                                 to the contract's over one vector set; flows lane widened
packs/*/tasks/*/task.json        28 declarations gain the field — 23 schedule, 5 request
packs/claudinite-growth/skills/  writing-tasks: the two fields, and the inert-cadence rule
docs/                            DESIGN §5 and §15.33 (both rejected alternatives, with the
                                 ground each lost on), preconditions design, S79
```

3347 tests green, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking. Rebased onto main, which had cut `claudinite-tasks 60906.7` while this waited — that put the migration record's pinned version at or below every member's installed version, silently already-applied, so it's re-pinned to `60906.8` with a note to re-check it on every rebase. Main's rule I (#1785) was also passing a frequency string into a predicate this branch changed to a boolean, so it had stopped firing; three tests caught it.

CI is still running on the new head (`9a5f87b`); I'll act on the result when the event arrives rather than polling.

> ⚠️ Still open: your review of PR #1733 ("lgtm" merges); CI in flight on `9a5f87b`; the simulator-coupling question from the last round; after merge, the verification and retrospective sub-issues of #1725, and #1732's `Blocked-by`.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

A task declares `trigger: schedule | request` — who mints an occurrence — and
`preconditions` says only what must then hold, judged identically whichever
asked. The cadence is a term over the task's own run history, so the engine
keeps no calendar and no schedule board: every tick asks every scheduled task,
a decline is a log line, and one live item per task is the only invariant.

`task:origin:manual` splits a pulled run of a declared task from somebody's own
issue adopted as the work item. `frequency` and `none` are retired behind a door
and the nightly update rewrites members' own declarations.

Closes #1731
Refs #1725

input.title: Check that a migration record's `version` is above its pack's current version
input.body:
A migration record names the version the bump will cut on `main` after its PR merges (#1726). It has to be strictly above every member's installed version, or a converged member reads the record as already applied and skips it — silently, with no error and no failing test, exactly the way a wrong count is silent.

Nothing checks this, and the convention races `main`'s own version bumps. On [#1733](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1733) it went wrong three times: written at `60906.5` while the pack was at `60906.4`, then `main` cut `60906.7` and later `60906.8` while the branch waited for review, each time leaving the record at or below the installed version. A code review caught the first; a re-read on rebase caught the other two. There is no reason the fourth would be caught.

**The check:** for every `packs/<pack>/migrations/*/migration.mjs`, its `version` must be strictly greater than that pack's `pack.mjs` `version`. Both are string-typed dotted identifiers, so compare them as the version comparator does and never as floats (`60906.10` and `60906.1` are different versions and the same number).

Blocking, and relevance-first on a record existing — a repo carrying none is a no-op. It is a two-artifact claim that can drift independently, which is what a check is for; the record's own comment asking a human to re-read it on every rebase is the prose version of the same rule, and can go once this lands.

input.commit_title: Scheduling is the task's own precondition; the scheduler keeps no state (#1733)
input.commit_message:
A task declares `trigger: schedule | request` — who mints an occurrence — and
`preconditions` says only what must then hold, judged identically whichever
asked. The cadence is a term over the task's own run history, so the engine
keeps no calendar and no schedule board: every tick asks every scheduled task,
a decline is a log line, and one live item per task is the only invariant.

`task:origin:manual` splits a pulled run of a declared task from somebody's own
issue adopted as the work item. `frequency` and `none` are retired behind a door,
`trigger` is derived for a declaration stating none, and the nightly update
writes both into members' own declarations.

Closes #1731
Refs #1725
